messages:
Priya: Quick sync: we keep seeing spikes of partial streams where client cancels but upstream keeps producing for ~200ms. Need a clean handoff token to coordinate cancel/hedge owners so we don't double-bill or double-cache.
Noah: Is this the same phenomenon as delayed hedges (fanout wins after client abort)? We should ensure winner selection happens BEFORE we propagate billing events.
Diego: Happy path: client opens stream -> gateway issues short-lived handoff token to upstream(s). Token ties the in-memory lease to the stream-id and owning attempt. On cancel, gateway sends token-revocation to all upstreams; they should stop producing if they honor the token.
Hannah: Who owns the token lifecycle? Gateway, or the ingress load-balancer? I'd prefer gateway to own issuance + TTL to keep logic centralized.
Priya: Gateway owns it. Token semantics: opaque string, expires in X ms (configurable per-tenant), includes attempt number. Header: `x-rw-handoff` (opaque).
Noah: TTL decision: we need two knobs: a short TTL for low-latency streams (~150ms) and a longer grace TTL for longpoll/batch streams (~5s). Can be per-route config.
Diego: What about hedging? If we fanout to N upstreams, only one token is 'active'. Others get `x-rw-handoff: standby`. When a winner emerges, gateway flips an explicit `x-rw-handoff-winner` callback to all to indicate who owns the canonical result.
Hannah: Callbacks multiply network chatter. Could embed winner flag in terminal-event instead (trailers/final chunk). But winner needs to be decided before we stop other upstreams producing to save compute.
Priya: Compromise: winner decision via quick control message on internal control plane channel (RPC), not customer data plane. We already have a control stream between gateway and upstream proxies. Use that for rapid winner notification; reserve trailers for public signal.
Noah: Edge case: upstream ignores control message (legacy). Gateway must still be safe: if we can't confirm stop, we accept potential wasted tokens but ensure billing attribution is gateway-side (gateway credits winner, debits others as transient).
Diego: Also need backpressure semantics: client write pace could be faster than upstream consumption. We should propagate a `prefetch_window` concept to upstreams describing how many tokens/frames to precompute. Header: `x-rw-prefetch-window: 3` (default 1). Upstream may pre-render up to N frames but must respect handoff revoke.
Hannah: Prefetch helps latency, but increases wasted work on cancels. Make prefetch adaptive: gateway measures cancellation rate per-route and adjusts window automatically.
Priya: Observability: emit events `handoff_issued`, `handoff_revoked`, `handoff_winner`, plus `prefetch_used`. Capture `attempt_count` and `tenant_id` (hashed) in events.
Noah: Security: tokens must be HMAC-signed and short-lived. Do not allow clients to forge or replay them. Gateway should rotate signing keys per-region.
Diego: Implementation detail: store token lease in an in-memory LRU keyed by stream-id with TTL. For long-lived streams, renew on heartbeat. If token store evicts early, revoke to upstreams.
Hannah: For HTTP/1.1 clients we won't have trailers. Terminal-event: final JSON chunk {"stream_status":"ok","prefetch_used":2,"winner":"true"}. For h2/h3 prefer trailers `stream-status` + metadata.
Priya: Backwards compatibility: if upstream doesn't understand `x-rw-prefetch-window` treat as 0. If doesn't honor `x-rw-handoff`, gateway falls back to best-effort cancel (stop reading socket).
Noah: Billing alignment: do not increment billable tokens until gateway marks a frame as consumed by winner. Upstream should report produced frames as 'speculative' unless they hold winning token.
Diego: This implies upstreams must mark frames with `speculative:true` vs `final:true`. We'll add a frame header `rw-frame-final: 0|1`.
Hannah: Complexity grows. Add a feature flag to roll this out: `handoff-token-enabled` per-tenant. Start with a handful of high-volume customers.
infra-bot: NOTE: staging WAF rules updated to allow x-rw-handoff and x-rw-prefetch-window. Rollout window: Thursday 02:00 UTC.
Priya: Action items: 1) gate flag + per-tenant knobs 2) implement token issuance + control-plane callback 3) add prefetch-window adaptive controller 4) update billing pipeline to wait for winner ack 5) e2e tests for ignored-revoke case.
Noah: I'll sketch RFC with sequence diagrams and sample header schemas.
Diego: I'll prototype token store and revoke RPC.
Hannah: I'll own observability + feature flag gating.
Priya: Thanks all. Quick note: be conservative with defaults (prefetch_window=1, token_ttl=200ms). We'll tune after canary. :rocket:
